label: Wavelength-insensitive 2x2 MZ electro-optic switch (two-DC broadband 50 % couplers, 200 um p-i-n carrier-injection phase shifter), Si rib
core_material: Si 220 nm SOI rib, 500 nm wide, 170 nm etch leaving a 50 nm slab (lateral p-i-n in the slab, p+/n+ 1e21 cm-3 about 500 nm from the core, NiSi contacts, W plugs, Cu interconnect); fully etched access wires (STI module) with SiOxNy couplers over inverse tapers; 2 um BOX, 200 mm 10 ohm cm p-type SOI
cladding: SiO2 (deposited, CMP-planarized) and dielectric stack; thickness not stated
process_name: subset of IBM front-end CMOS process modules, 90 nm ground rules, 193 nm DUV lithography, 8 levels
notes: Single 2x2 switch element (D158). Broadband 50 % couplers = two directional couplers (design power coupling 0.4 and 0.8, lengths 15 / 24.5 um) with a 0.54 pi phase delay (160 nm length imbalance) in a point-symmetric MZ (p.4); the couplers are not characterized separately (geometry only, no row). Phase-shifter length 200 um (p.3). Measured center of the 110 nm window 1530 nm vs 1550 nm design (bend coupling not included in the design, p.6): no center_wavelength parameter for switch_fabric. Not entered per the coordinator brief (modulator metrics, EO atlas): on-state voltage Von = 1 V (+/-0.01 V, steady state, Ion 3.5 +/- 0.1 mA, p.7), 1.02 V (+/-0.02 V, pulsed, Ion 3.1 +/- 0.1 mA, p.8), 0.3 V peak-to-peak swing on a 0.87 V bias, VpiL about 0.06 V mm (p.8); 30 / 50 C on-state bias 0.99 / 0.97 V, 3.3 / 3.0 mA (p.9). On-state FCA-only loss (spectra normalized to the off-state output sum): T11 0.9 +/- 0.2 dB, T22 0.9 +/- 0.4 dB measured, 0.8 dB simulated (p.7, p.4 Table 1): loss of the EO phase shifter, kept in notes (lu2016a precedent); the on-state total IL is entered. p-i-n series resistance 8 +/- 2 ohm, 1.6 +/- 0.4 ohm mm (p.7): series_resistance_ohm not allowed for switch_fabric. Switching energy 6 fJ/bit (p.10) rests on an assumed 2 nm / 10 Gb/s WDM load: not entered. Fab: the acknowledgment states the devices were fabricated at the Microelectronics Research Laboratory (MRL) of the IBM T. J. Watson Research Center (p.10) and Sec. 3 states the fabrication used IBM front-end CMOS process modules (p.5); all authors IBM T.J. Watson Research Center -> org_ibm_watson. MRL is IBM's internal lab, not a shared facility (D404 analogue): facility empty.
